question.problem: Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=2{x}^{2}-2$ whose tangent has a slope of $2.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}-2.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}-2) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\  & =2\cdot 2x-0 \\  & =4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=2$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =2 \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $2$ at the point where $x=\frac{1}{2}.$
